name: Flattery
definition: Praise aimed at a person's competence, expertise, or standing, offered to loosen their discretion before a follow-up question.
mechanism: Praise competence or standing so pride loosens discretion
recognition_cue: Praise out of proportion to the setting; being cast as the expert
countermeasure: Acknowledge professionally, do not expand; notice praise that precedes a question

name: Provocation / feigned incredulity
definition: Displaying deliberate skepticism toward a claim so the target elaborates to prove it, or answers out of irritation at being doubted.
mechanism: Show disbelief so the target explains in detail or answers out of irritation
recognition_cue: Staged doubt that invites you to defend a claim
countermeasure: Stay composed; do not prove capability with detail

name: Deliberate false statement
definition: An intentionally incorrect statement offered so the target supplies the accurate version in the act of correcting it.
mechanism: State something wrong so the target corrects it with the truth
recognition_cue: An obvious error that seems set up for your correction
countermeasure: Resist correcting; ask a clarifying question instead

name: Criticism
definition: Criticism of the target's work, employer, or a rival, offered to provoke a defensive rebuttal that discloses detail.
mechanism: Attack the target's work, employer, or rival to draw a defensive rebuttal
recognition_cue: An urge to defend what you are proud of
countermeasure: Recognize the ego-bait; decline to defend with specifics

name: One-upper / can-you-top-this
definition: A modest or exaggerated claim offered first so the target feels a competitive pull to top it with a larger, more specific one.
mechanism: Share a lesser claim to bait a larger one
recognition_cue: A competitive pull to top a story or figure
countermeasure: Do not reciprocate the escalation

name: Feigned ignorance
definition: A pose of ignorance about a subject the target knows well, meant to draw out an explanatory answer aimed at a supposed novice.
mechanism: Play ignorant so the target teaches
recognition_cue: A pull to instruct a supposed novice
countermeasure: Refer to public documentation; do not fill gaps for strangers

name: Confidential bait
definition: A disclosure framed as confidential, offered first so the target feels invited to trade a confidence of their own.
mechanism: Share a supposed confidence to trigger a reciprocal one
recognition_cue: "Just between us" openers
countermeasure: Do not match confidences

name: Quid pro quo / volunteering / trading confidences
definition: An offer of a fact, favor, or personal disclosure made first so the target feels a social debt to reciprocate with information of their own.
mechanism: Give a fact or favor first so the target feels owed
recognition_cue: An unsolicited disclosure tied to a follow-up ask
countermeasure: Recognize the felt debt is not real; decline to trade

name: Good listener
definition: Sustained, warm attention and active listening used to keep the target talking and steer the conversation toward a topic of interest.
mechanism: Warm, patient attention that keeps the target talking
recognition_cue: Unusual attentiveness paired with topic-steering
countermeasure: Watch conversational momentum; limit work talk with new contacts

name: Mutual interest
definition: A manufactured sense of shared interest or background, built quickly so cooperation and disclosure feel like a natural next step.
mechanism: Manufacture shared ground so cooperation feels natural
recognition_cue: Fast rapport over convenient common interests
countermeasure: Question whether shared interest justifies disclosure

name: Mirroring
definition: Matching the target's body language, tone, and phrasing to build unconscious rapport that keeps the conversation open.
mechanism: Match body language and echo phrases to build rapport
recognition_cue: Subtle imitation that lingers on one topic
countermeasure: Note the synchrony; keep professional distance

name: Assumed knowledge
definition: Speech that presumes the listener already knows the sensitive detail, so confirming or correcting it feels like the natural response.
mechanism: Speak as if already inside so confirming feels natural
recognition_cue: Statements that assume facts you never shared
countermeasure: Verify what they actually know before responding; do not correct a false assumption

name: Bracketing
definition: A deliberately wide or wrong numeric range offered so the target narrows it toward the true figure.
mechanism: Offer a high/low range to bait the exact figure
recognition_cue: A wrong numeric range about your work
countermeasure: Refuse to narrow the range or confirm an estimate

name: Leading question / embedded presumption
definition: A question built around a hidden presumption, so any direct answer accepts a fact the target never actually confirmed.
mechanism: Ask a question whose answer must accept a presumption
recognition_cue: Yes/no framing loaded with an assumption
countermeasure: Reject the frame; answer on your own terms

name: Macro to micro (to macro)
definition: A conversation that opens broad, narrows to a single sensitive detail, then widens out again so the narrowing goes unnoticed.
mechanism: Start broad, funnel to the specific, then broaden again to disguise it
recognition_cue: A conversation that narrows to one detail then eases off
countermeasure: Notice the funnel; redirect

name: Oblique reference / analogy
definition: Discussion of a related or comparable system, meant to draw the target into using their own work as an unwitting reference point.
mechanism: Discuss a related system so the target uses their own work as the reference
recognition_cue: Talk about an adjacent topic that keeps circling back to yours
countermeasure: Do not elaborate; avoid comparative analysis of your systems

name: Quote reported facts
definition: A citation of already-public data, used as a springboard toward the unpublished detail that would confirm or extend it.
mechanism: Cite published data to draw out the unpublished
recognition_cue: "The press release said X, so I assume Y?"
countermeasure: Do not fill the gap past what is already public

name: Word repetition
definition: The target's own key word or phrase, echoed back as a prompt for further elaboration on it.
mechanism: Echo the target's key term to prompt elaboration
recognition_cue: Your own phrase repeated back as a prompt
countermeasure: Notice the echo; stop expanding

name: Direct question / survey
definition: A blunt, direct question that relies on the social norm that a question posed deserves an answer.
mechanism: Blunt asks that bank on the norm that questions get answered
recognition_cue: Immediate bluntness about specifics
countermeasure: Pause; judge whether disclosure is appropriate

name: Questionnaires and surveys
definition: A survey or questionnaire that buries sensitive questions among benign ones under a plausible cover purpose.
mechanism: Bury target questions among benign ones under a plausible purpose
recognition_cue: A survey mixing harmless items with work specifics
countermeasure: Answer only public items; refer to the security office

name: Ruse interview
definition: A fabricated interview, often posing as a recruiter or headhunter, staged to justify probing questions about recent work.
mechanism: Pose as a recruiter or headhunter to justify probing
recognition_cue: An unsolicited recruiter pressing on recent project detail
countermeasure: Verify identity and authorization through an independent channel

name: Target associates / target the outsider
definition: An approach routed through a relative or colleague, or questions about a group the target does not belong to, to reach information indirectly.
mechanism: Approach through a relative or colleague, or ask about a group you are not in
recognition_cue: Questions routed through people close to you
countermeasure: Protect third-party information

name: Exploiting the urge to complain
definition: An invitation to vent about work frustration, used to surface setbacks, staffing gaps, and delays the target would not otherwise volunteer.
mechanism: Prompt a gripe to surface setbacks, staffing gaps, and delays
recognition_cue: An invitation to vent about work pressure
countermeasure: Do not discuss schedules, staffing, or resource constraints with unauthorized people

name: Paper review / academic solicitation
definition: An unsolicited request to review a paper or proposal, framed to draw the target's sensitive expertise into the response.
mechanism: Request peer review so the target applies sensitive knowledge
recognition_cue: An unsolicited review request touching your program
countermeasure: Consult the security office before accepting; release only authorized material

name: Offering assistance
definition: Genuine, unsolicited help offered to a target, used to surface their interests and needs and to build a sense of obligation.
mechanism: Offer genuine help to surface the target's interests (FM 34-60)
recognition_cue: Help that arrives with an interest in your work
countermeasure: Recognize the obligation chain; report offered inducements

name: Hypothetical situation
definition: A hypothetical scenario built directly on something the target just said, inviting them to reason through sensitive ground as if it were speculation.
mechanism: Pose a hypothetical tied to the target's own idea (FM 34-60)
recognition_cue: A "what if" built on something you just said
countermeasure: Do not engage the hypothetical on sensitive ground

name: Setting manipulation
definition: A deliberate shift of the conversation to a relaxed, off-work setting, sometimes involving alcohol, to lower the target's guard.
mechanism: Move the exchange to relaxed, off-work surroundings, sometimes with alcohol
recognition_cue: A push toward private, informal, unobservable settings
countermeasure: Treat off-site chats with the same guard as the office

name: The Scharff technique
definition: A structured approach that pairs a friendly, non-confrontational tone with the impression the interviewer already knows most of what is being discussed, drawing confirmation or denial without ever asking directly.
mechanism: A friendly approach, an illusion of already knowing it all, never pressing, floating claims to confirm or deny, and downplaying what you reveal
recognition_cue: A pleasant conversation where the other person seems to know most of it and never actually asks; you leave feeling you gave away nothing
countermeasure: Recognize the profile; note that "they already know it" is a trap belief. Awareness alone is weak here, so this needs practiced response, not just a warning

name: Direct
definition: Plain, pertinent questions asked without pretext, historically the single most effective interrogation approach.
mechanism: Plain pertinent questions; historically 85 to 95 percent effective
recognition_cue: Direct questions with no pretext
countermeasure: No obligation to answer; declining is the counter

name: Incentive
definition: A material or emotional reward, or the removal of a negative, offered contingent on the source providing information.
mechanism: Trade a material or emotional reward, or removal of a negative, for information
recognition_cue: Offers or favors made contingent on your talking
countermeasure: Refuse the obligation chain; report inducements (maps to AR 381-12 3-1i)

name: Emotional Love
definition: An approach that directs the source's genuine love of family, homeland, or comrades toward cooperating with the interviewer.
mechanism: Direct love of family, homeland, or comrades toward cooperation
recognition_cue: Talk returns to family or comrades and what you could do "for them"
countermeasure: See the manufactured link between an emotional object and disclosure

name: Emotional Hate
definition: An approach that builds on the source's genuine hate or desire for revenge until it overrides their judgment about disclosure.
mechanism: Build on genuine hate or desire for revenge until it overrides judgment
recognition_cue: Someone amplifying your grievances and offering revenge through disclosure
countermeasure: Note that grievance is being weaponized to bypass judgment

name: Fear-Up
definition: A fear identified or created in the source, with its removal offered in exchange for cooperation.
mechanism: Identify or create a fear, then link its removal to cooperation
recognition_cue: Threat framing, specific or vague, with talking as the exit
countermeasure: Recognize the fear-then-relief structure; doctrine notes overshooting makes the source unresponsive

name: Fear-Down
definition: A reduction of an existing fear, positioning the interviewer as a protector the source feels indebted to.
mechanism: Reduce an existing fear so the source feels indebted to the "protector"
recognition_cue: A calming interlocutor after a stressful event
countermeasure: Emotional relief is not a reason to disclose

name: Pride and Ego-Up
definition: Sustained flattery aimed at low self-esteem, meant to draw the source into talking to earn credit or recognition.
mechanism: Flatter low self-esteem into talking to gain credit
recognition_cue: Sustained flattery, then rising technical curiosity
countermeasure: This is the interrogation cousin of elicitation flattery; the drilldown is the tell

name: Pride and Ego-Down
definition: A direct attack on the source's ego or competence, meant to provoke disclosure offered in self-justification.
mechanism: Attack the ego so the source reveals information to justify itself
recognition_cue: Belittling of your ability or loyalty, inviting you to set the record straight
countermeasure: Do not take the bait to justify yourself

name: Futility
definition: An argument that resistance is hopeless, meant to convince the source that cooperation is the only remaining option.
mechanism: Convince the source resistance is hopeless
recognition_cue: "Everyone else already talked" / "your side has lost"
countermeasure: The "everybody cooperated" claim is the signature; futility alone rarely works

name: We Know All
definition: An implication that the interviewer already knows everything the source could offer, meant to make disclosure feel harmless.
mechanism: Imply all the source's information is already known
recognition_cue: Interviewer acts bored, finishes your sentences, implies you are redundant
countermeasure: A source who says "then you don't need me" defeats it

name: File and Dossier
definition: A padded or fabricated file referenced, but never shown, to imply the interviewer already knows more than they do.
mechanism: A padded file implies more is known than is
recognition_cue: A thick "file on you" referenced but never handed over
countermeasure: Depends on the source's naivete; the We Know All refusal logic applies

name: Establish Your Identity
definition: A false insistence that the source is a different, wanted person, meant to provoke an over-explanation offered to clear their name.
mechanism: Insist the source is a wanted person so they over-explain to clear themselves
recognition_cue: Accusation of being someone else, pressing you to prove who you are
countermeasure: "Proving your identity" is the extraction vector; volunteer nothing beyond required ID

name: Repetition
definition: The same question and answer, repeated until boredom or fatigue loosens the source into a more candid response.
mechanism: Repeat question and answer until boredom produces candor
recognition_cue: The same question and answer echoed repeatedly
countermeasure: Ineffective against self-control; it can let you regain composure

name: Rapid Fire
definition: Overlapping, rapid questions meant to induce a contradiction, which the interviewer then confronts the source with.
mechanism: Overlapping questions induce contradiction, then confront it
recognition_cue: Interrupting questions; being told you contradicted yourself
countermeasure: The trap is the urge to reconcile on demand; slow down and decline

name: Silent
definition: Deliberate, prolonged silence used as pressure to make the source fill the gap with speech.
mechanism: Silence as pressure to make the source fill it
recognition_cue: Prolonged deliberate silence and eye contact
countermeasure: Silence is a prompt, not an obligation

name: Change of Scenery
definition: A shift to an informal setting where the questioning continues quietly under the appearance of a relaxed conversation.
mechanism: Move to an informal setting where questioning quietly continues
recognition_cue: A shift to a relaxed venue where questions keep coming
countermeasure: Bridges into elicitation; the venue does not change what is sensitive

name: Mutt and Jeff
definition: A harsh interviewer followed by a sympathetic one, meant to make the source bond with and disclose to the second.
mechanism: A harsh then a sympathetic interviewer; the source bonds with the second
recognition_cue: Classic good-cop/bad-cop pairing
countermeasure: The friendly one runs the same objective; requires O-6 approval in doctrine

name: False Flag
definition: A false claim of nationality or affiliation, meant to convince the source a friendlier third party is doing the questioning.
mechanism: Convince the source a friendlier third country is questioning them
recognition_cue: Claimed nationality or affiliation designed to make you feel safer
countermeasure: Verify who is actually asking; misrepresented affiliation is the manipulation

name: Pretexting
definition: A fabricated scenario or identity constructed to justify a request for information or access.
mechanism: A fabricated scenario or identity justifies a request
recognition_cue: A complete backstory paired with pressure to skip verification
countermeasure: Verify identity through an independently sourced channel, never the contact details in the request

name: Phishing
definition: Deceptive mass email or a lookalike site, built to solicit data or an action from whoever falls for it.
mechanism: Deceptive mass email or sites solicit data or action
recognition_cue: Unsolicited requests, lookalike domains, urgency
countermeasure: Phishing-resistant MFA, filtering, verify links via known numbers, report

name: Spear-phishing
definition: Phishing personalized with open-source detail about the target's role, so the message reads as legitimately informed.
mechanism: Phishing personalized from OSINT
recognition_cue: A message that knows too much about your role and uses it
countermeasure: Same as phishing plus reduced public detail and out-of-band verification

name: Whaling
definition: Spear-phishing aimed specifically at executives, using urgency and confidentiality framing to route around normal process.
mechanism: Spear-phishing aimed at executives
recognition_cue: "Urgent and confidential" requests routing around process
countermeasure: Executive impersonation controls, mandatory verification workflows

name: Vishing
definition: Voice-call social engineering, often using spoofed caller ID, to extract information or codes over the phone.
mechanism: Voice-call social engineering, VoIP caller-ID spoofing
recognition_cue: Urgency by phone, discouraged callbacks, requests for codes
countermeasure: Call back on a known number; out-of-band confirmation for resets and transfers

name: Smishing
definition: A text message carrying a malicious link or callback number, disguised as an account or delivery alert.
mechanism: SMS carrying links or callback numbers
recognition_cue: Unexpected texts with links or "alerts"
countermeasure: Do not click; verify via the official app or known number

name: Baiting
definition: An object or offer, such as a dropped USB drive or a free file, designed to bait curiosity into a compromising action.
mechanism: Curiosity or reward (a dropped USB, a free file) induces a compromising action
recognition_cue: Found media, "too good" offers, unsolicited exclusive files
countermeasure: Prohibit unknown USB media; block autorun; training

name: Quid pro quo (cyber)
definition: Unsolicited technical help offered in trade for account access or data.
mechanism: Offered "help" traded for access or data
recognition_cue: Unsolicited IT-support offers conditioned on access
countermeasure: Verify support contacts through the internal help desk

name: Tailgating / piggybacking
definition: Following an authorized person through a controlled door without independently badging in.
mechanism: Follow an authorized person through a controlled door
recognition_cue: Someone without a badge follows or asks you to hold the door
countermeasure: Badge per person, challenge culture, visitor escort

name: Watering-hole
definition: Compromise of a website the target group is known to frequent, so a trusted destination becomes the delivery point.
mechanism: Compromise a site the target group frequents
recognition_cue: Hard to see; unexpected prompts on a trusted industry site
countermeasure: Patching, browser isolation, EDR, egress monitoring

name: Business email compromise
definition: A compromised or lookalike executive or vendor email account, used to redirect a payment or sensitive data.
mechanism: Compromised or lookalike executive/vendor email redirects payment or data
recognition_cue: Last-minute change to wire instructions; almost-correct sender
countermeasure: Out-of-band verification of any payment change; report to ic3.gov

name: Requests for information
definition: An unsolicited request for information arriving from an unknown or unverified, potentially foreign, source.
mechanism: Unsolicited requests from unknown or foreign sources
recognition_cue: A request for information that arrives from someone whose identity or affiliation cannot be confirmed
countermeasure: Verify identity and authorization before responding; do not respond if unverifiable; report

name: Solicitation and marketing of services
definition: The placement of foreign personnel inside a business relationship through a joint venture, distributorship, or service offer.
mechanism: Placing foreign personnel via ventures or service offers
recognition_cue: A foreign national embedded in a joint venture, distributorship, or service contract with access beyond the deal's actual scope
countermeasure: Review outgoing documents, give foreign representatives stand-alone computers, limit sharing to the venture scope, build a Technology Control Plan

name: Suspicious network activity
definition: Hacking, malware, or phishing used against an organization's network, the fastest-growing of the collection methods.
mechanism: The fastest-growing method: hacking, malware, phishing
recognition_cue: Unexplained system activity, an unfamiliar process, or an unsolicited link or attachment tied to a work topic
countermeasure: Audit systems, do not rely on firewalls alone, report intrusion attempts, do not click unknown links

name: Academic solicitation
definition: The use of students, professors, or researchers to collect sensitive information under the cover of legitimate academic activity.
mechanism: Students, professors, and researchers used to collect under academic pretense
recognition_cue: An unsolicited research collaboration, review request, or conference invitation from an unverified academic contact
countermeasure: Treat unsolicited academic requests with suspicion, respond only to verified individuals, release only authorized information

name: Foreign visits
definition: Information gathering carried out during an official or unofficial visit to a facility.
mechanism: Suspicious gathering during facility visits
recognition_cue: A visitor who strays from the planned route, lingers near controlled areas, or asks questions outside the visit's stated purpose
countermeasure: Coordinate with DCSA before the visit, brief hosts and escorts, walk the route, bar recording devices

name: Conferences, conventions, and trade shows
definition: The use of conferences, conventions, and trade shows to link a targeted program to the people who know it best.
mechanism: Linking targeted programs to knowledgeable people
recognition_cue: A conference contact whose questions track your program rather than the show's general subject matter
countermeasure: Brief travelers on elicitation response, display mock-ups rather than real equipment, debrief attendees
